system_prompt: /no_think You write to an exact spec, matching an existing codebase's conventions exactly. Output ONLY the requested file contents in the exact structure asked for — no markdown fences, no explanation before, between, or after the files.
task:
The reference files show the existing pattern for a REST resource in this Express app: route handlers + validation in src/resources/users.js, its test file in test/users.test.js (using node:test + supertest + assert/strict), and the shared in-memory store helper in src/store.js. Follow that exact pattern — same import style, same validation error-message phrasing, same route structure (GET list, GET by id with 404, POST with 201/400, PUT with partial validation and 404, DELETE with 204/404), same test style and assertions — to add two new resources.

Resource 1: 'projects'. Schema: Project { id (auto), name (required non-empty string), description (optional string), ownerId (required, must be a positive integer), createdAt (auto) }. Export the router as projectsRouter and the store as projectsStore.

Resource 2: 'tasks'. Schema: Task { id (auto), title (required non-empty string), description (optional string), status (optional string; if provided must be one of 'todo', 'in_progress', 'done', reject with a validation error otherwise; if omitted on create, default to 'todo'), projectId (required, must be a positive integer), assigneeId (optional, must be a positive integer if provided, may be omitted or null), createdAt (auto) }. Export the router as tasksRouter and the store as tasksStore.

Output exactly four files, each preceded by a line containing only one of these exact markers (including the === on both sides), in this order:
===FILE: src/resources/projects.js===
===FILE: test/projects.test.js===
===FILE: src/resources/tasks.js===
===FILE: test/tasks.test.js===

Each test file should cover at least: successful creation, a validation-failure case specific to that resource's schema (e.g. invalid status for tasks, non-integer ownerId for projects), 404 on unknown id, list, update, and delete — matching the coverage style of test/users.test.js.
